ai.description: This toad reaches 8–10 cm. It is yellowish-brown with black-tipped cranial crests and warts. A prominent, continuous black ridge surrounds the snout and eyes, distinguishing it from other species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Duttaphrynus melanostictus* is the presence of prominent, black-tipped cranial crests that surround the upper eyelids.
ai.habitat: The Javanese toad inhabits lowland areas, including gardens, agricultural fields, and disturbed forests, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Javanese toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for insects and other small invertebrates across diverse habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus melanostictus* is oviparous, breeding primarily during the monsoon (June–September). Females lay thousands of eggs in long, gelatinous strings in water.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Javanese toad occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the Himalayan foothills and plains of states like Assam, West Bengal, and Meghalaya, up to 1,500m elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Javanese Toad emits a high-pitched, rhythmic, and repetitive trill, typically heard near stagnant water bodies or human-altered habitats during the rainy season.
